title: Hatshepsut's obelisk inscription dedicating it to her father Amun

tellings.quote: and I've read the translated hieroglyphs and she said she said um she said [clears throat] as for this obelisk it's something I'm paraphrasing but it's like as for this obelisk I erected this uh from um from electrum

plain: The ancient Egyptian ruler Hatshepsut, according to the researcher Luke Caverns, had an obelisk at Karnak inscribed to say it was dedicated to her father, the god Amun, and made with electrum, a mix of gold and silver. Caverns tells Michels he has read the translated hieroglyphs and gives the inscription from memory, saying he is paraphrasing: "as for this obelisk, I erected this from electrum." He offers it as a clue that the old monuments are not what we think, though his wording is his own summary, not the inscription's exact text.
